_comment: One source for video players, VideoObject markup and the video sitemap. durationSeconds is measured from the delivered MP4 with ffprobe; captions and chapters are WebVTT. Preserve original upload dates when updating metadata.

swift-interop.name: Osprey exports and externs: one app for the Mac and iPhone with Swift
swift-interop.description: A four-minute tutorial. Osprey exports compile to a C header that Swift calls, Swift @_cdecl functions become Osprey externs, an effect keeps the boundary testable, and one Xcode target ships the app to the Mac and the iPhone. Then the Osprey tests, and an edit to the hidden-files rule that they catch.
swift-interop.posterAlt: Osprey + Swift title card with the Osprey bird, the Osprey Storage app icon and the words One app, Mac and iPhone

profiler.name: Profiling Osprey programs in VS Code: CPU, memory and leaks
profiler.description: A four-minute tutorial. Read two sample programs and predict where the time goes, then profile them in VS Code, read the flame graph and the heat on the source, attach to a running program, compare Osprey's memory backends, and check for leaks with ARC.
profiler.posterAlt: The Profiling Osprey title card with the Osprey bird and the words CPU, memory, leaks, in VS Code

package-manager.name: Add and remove Osprey packages in VS Code
package-manager.description: Browse Osprey packages, review audit warnings, add and verify a dependency, then remove it through the VS Code package workspace.
package-manager.posterAlt: The VS Code Command Palette with Osprey: Manage Packages selected.

chromecast-from-mac.name: Osprey effects for I/O: a Chromecast sender you can test with no TV
chromecast-from-mac.description: A seven-minute tutorial. Write every byte of input and output as one Osprey effect, return failures as Result, answer the effect with a real handler in the app and a fake one in tests. The worked example is the @osprey/chromecast package and the casting player: discovery, the CAST v2 frame format, serving the file, the app's adapter, eight tests with no TV, and an edit the tests catch.
chromecast-from-mac.posterAlt: Title card with the Osprey bird and the words Chromecast from a Mac to a TV

static-typing-python.name: Type inference in the Osprey Python flavor: static types with no hints
static-typing-python.description: A five-minute tutorial. Python-style code with no annotations, type-checked before it runs: a small sample, the error a wrong argument gives, records, Result and match, effects, and the @osprey/chromecast package checked against CPython. Then one edit that mixes two return types, caught at compile time.
static-typing-python.posterAlt: Title card with the Osprey bird and the words Static typing for Python, no hints

ui-testing-by-label.name: Testing Osprey apps by label with @osprey/uitest
ui-testing-by-label.description: A six-minute tutorial. Where a control's role and label come from, how @osprey/native builds the accessibility tree, how @osprey/uitest finds controls by label and drives them with real pointer events, a whole journey from the casting player's tests, and an edit that renames one label and fails three tests.
ui-testing-by-label.posterAlt: Title card with the Osprey bird and the words An accessibility tree agents can drive

rust-ui-framework-without-rust.name: GPUI apps in Osprey: a Rust UI framework without writing Rust
rust-ui-framework-without-rust.description: A five-minute tutorial. GPUI's own painting example ported to Osprey, file by file: the two-function boundary the Rust host calls, the store, the drawing rules and the view. Then its tests and headless self-test with no window, and an edit to the dash pattern that one test catches.
rust-ui-framework-without-rust.posterAlt: Title card with the Osprey bird and the words A Rust UI framework, no Rust

agent-native.name: Osprey Agent: a native coding agent in action
agent-native.description: Watch the real macOS SwiftUI agent, recorded live: it runs failing calculator tests, fixes the code, verifies the fix and shows the corrected code, with native controls and AOT Osprey application logic.
agent-native.posterAlt: Osprey Agent, recorded live, working through a calculator fix with its native usage inspector

native-bridge.name: The Osprey Native bridge: one frame in shared memory
native-bridge.description: A seven-minute code tutorial. One typeDiagram model defines fixed rows that an Osprey app writes into shared memory; the SwiftUI, GPUI, WinUI, Android and VS Code hosts lease, check and read them in place, with no serialization. Then Tally's reference host runs, and a one-word change that it catches.
native-bridge.posterAlt: Title card reading One frame, shared memory, with the Osprey bird and the words Osprey Native, the bridge

light-orchestra.name: Light Orchestra: play your Mac from your phone
light-orchestra.description: A phone's controller page plays the Light Orchestra app live: slide for notes, add fingers for chords, switch between four instruments and shape echo and reverb. Every sound is what the native app synthesised in Osprey, recorded with it.
light-orchestra.posterAlt: The Light Orchestra controller page with a glowing touch on its musical ribbon
